newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle futures end up on weather concerns.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle futures end up on weather concerns.

text.p: Weather concerns that developed on the forecast for another storm front moving through the southern Plains feedlot areas, coupled with technical support kept CME live cattle futures firm at the close, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.225 to 0.050 cent a lb higher with December up most at 67.025 cents after setting a 1-1/2 week high. Feeder cattle ended up 0.475 to 0.100 cents paced by January at 66.150 cents. Both contracts closed early at 1200 CST/1800 GMT in continued observance of the Thanksgiving holiday.
Storms moving through the Texas/Oklahoma panhandle area and into Midwest feedlot areas prompted much of the demand in live cattle.

There is concern over weight gains at feedlots, especially since feedlots are already current and choice cattle supplies are tight. The poor weather would extend time that cattle would have to be on feed to reach market weight, traders said.
Technical strength was also cited in live cattle futures. December filled a gap on the charts before running into light profit taking resistance, sources said.
RBH, Refco, Prudential Securities, Cargill Investor Services and locals bought December early. Spreaders bought December and sold February, pit sources said.
